title: Cliffnotes for manager sync — evidence, micro-asks, examples
content:
Purpose and framing:
- keep this <5 min to read before 1:1; bring 2–3 concrete asks + 1 win + 1 blocker.
- goal: surface impact, make it easy to say yes/no, show signals not arguments.

Top priorities for next sync (one-line):
1) Get approval for 0.5 FTE budget reallocation to onboarding experiments (Q2 pilot).
2) Start 6-week micro-eval for new manager interview rubric (metrics + panel).
3) Align on promotion criteria clarification for IC4→IC5 (ask: draft to share with Eng leads).

Quick evidence bites (two-liners I can read out):
- Onboarding time to first PR: median 22 days (Dec 2025), down from 28 after last onboarding doc edits — early sign onboarding docs helped, but still heavy variance for platform hires.
- New manager rubric pilot cohort (n=8): average panel score improvement +0.45 vs baseline in 3-month follow-up; anecdote: SRE rotation feedback shows faster trust calibration.
- Promotion backlogs: 14 pending calibration notes tagged with lack of role clarity; 60% of those are from eng teams with ambiguous IC4 expectations.

Three one-line claims I want to make (prep scripts):
- "Small investments in hands-on onboarding will cut time-to-first-PR by at least 20% for infra hires; that reduces long-term context ramp cost."
- "The current manager rubric leaves room for bias at the 'gives-feedback' bar; proposed clarifications remove two ambiguous checks."
- "If we don't prioritize the IC4→IC5 criteria this quarter, we'll see a bigger pile-up in Q3 calibration."

Micro-asks (easy to approve in sync):
- Approve $5k for external moderator for manager-rubric calibration session (one-off).
- Approve pilot headcount reallocation: 0.5 FTE from 'internal projects' to 'onboarding experiments' through end of Q2.
- Quick OK to ship draft promotion language to Eng leads for feedback by Mar 31.

Example phrasing for each ask (copy-paste):
- Budget: "I'd like approval for a $5k line item to bring an external moderator for a 2-hour calibration workshop; it reduces our calibration cycles and will be a one-time cost."
- Headcount reallocation: "Propose shifting 0.5 FTE from the internal projects bucket to run a time-boxed onboarding experiment for six weeks — measured by TTFPR and new hire NPS."
- Promotion language: "Can I have a go-ahead to circulate a draft to Eng leads for commentary (two-week feedback window)?"

Risks / objections I anticipate + one-sentence rebuttals:
- "We can’t spare headcount." -> "This is time-boxed 0.5 FTE and we expect measurable uplift in TTFPR that reduces support load downstream."
- "External moderator is expensive." -> "One-time cost vs multiple rounds of calibration; reduces manager time lost in re-runs."
- "Promotion language will spark long debates." -> "We’ll use this as a discussion starter and keep changes iterative; want to avoid indefinite blockers."

Red flags to surface (if asked):
- Persistent variance by hiring cohort (platform vs infra) suggests systemic onboarding mismatch.
- Two recent escalations where manager expectations weren't aligned with IC level — potential repeat if not addressed.

Open follow-ups I should own after sync:
- If approved: raise budget line in Concur + cc Finance (Aisha) within 48h.
- Draft and share promotion language on Confluence + ping Eng leads (Noah to help coordinate).
- If no headcount: propose alternative small experiment using agency fractional support (cost estimate to present next meeting).

Prep checklist (things to have ready before 1:1):
- One-pager (1/2 page) with metric table (TTFPR by cohort, pending promotions count) — link to Confluence page.
- Short script for each ask (see above).
- Snapshot of pilot cohort anecdotes (2 bullet quotes).
- Quick cost table: $5k moderator, $3k agency alternative, 0.5 FTE estimated salary delta.

Notes to self / talk cues:
- Start with 1 win (onboarding docs improvement) — builds credibility.
- Then ask: frame headcount as instrument to run tightly-scoped experiment.
- Emphasize measurables and stop conditions.
- If manager pushes back, offer a smaller, lower-risk alternative instead of deadlock.

Random scratch ideas (happy to iterate):
- Micro-mentorship pairing for platform hires first 30 days (shadow PR reviewer).
- Use tiny pulse surveys at day 7 and day 21 to capture early friction points.
- Bake a 'first PR checklist' into repo templates to remove doc-to-action gap.

Useful links (to copy into the Confluence page after sync):
- Confluence plan draft: https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/PE/onboarding-micro-experiments
- JIRA epic (tracking): JIRA-3421
- Pilot cohort notes (private doc): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcExample

Last-minute micro-reminders:
- Keep requests binary (approve/decline) — avoid long options list.
- Have a fallback 'no' plan to propose immediately if manager declines.
- Ask for a decision timeline if manager wants to defer.

---

End of scratchpad. Keep this private; will convert to a shareable one-pager if we get green light."
